cases.clinical_history: Patient Profile: N/A. Chief Complaint (CC): Left knee pain for more than a year. History of Present Illness (HPI): The pain in the left knee started suddenly and has been present for over a year. It is exacerbated by cold weather and exposure to cold water, and relieved by warmth. The pain is constant and does not increase with movement or activity. There is no swelling or stiffness unless exposed to cold, in which case stiffness lasts less than ten minutes. No giving way or locking of the knee. Systemic Enquiry / Review of Systems (ROS): No other joint issues, no back pain, no disc problems. Past Medical and Surgical History: Hypothyroidism, treated with 100 mg of thyroxine. Drug History: Takes thyroxine 100 mg daily. Family History: Aunt with lymphatic disease affecting her knees, undergoing radiation therapy. Family history of rheumatoid arthritis. No family history of diabetes or hypertension. Social History: Lives on the third floor with elevator access, uses stairs without difficulty. Non-smoker, occasional social use of hookah. Functional/Physiotherapy Relevance: No mobility limitations reported.
